name: Malaria Consortium, vitamin A with seasonal malaria chemoprevention in Bauchi, Nigeria (The Life You Can Save, 2025)
beneficiaries_note: The model's name: Malaria Consortium, vitamin A with seasonal malaria chemoprevention in Bauchi, Nigeria (The Life You Can Save, 2025).

missing_data.note: Measured: Malaria Consortium's baseline and endline coverage surveys of the integrated SMC and vitamin A cycle, and effects from trials of SMC (Mali) and the Cochrane review of vitamin A supplementation.

summary: Malaria Consortium added vitamin A capsules to the door-to-door seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) campaign in two areas of Bauchi state, Nigeria, in 2021, raising vitamin A coverage from 1% to 83%. The Life You Can Save credits the programme with the deaths averted by the vitamin A and SMC coverage added, at $1.18 a child, and estimates $11 per DALY averted. Our view values each child's death averted by age the site's way and counts only what the one round costed buys: a quarter of a season's SMC effect and half a year's vitamin A effect. The biggest uncertainties are the baseline SMC coverage the sheet assumes and how much protection one round gives.

Value of a death of a child under five averted, in healthy years
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The Life You Can Save counts a child's death averted as the child's remaining life expectancy at 2.5 years, discounted at 3%, about 28 years. The site values every death of a child under five the same way: GiveWell's moral weight (116.25 units of value), times the value-of-a-life slider, in healthy years at Your values' exchange rate (58 at the defaults).

rows.label: Share of a season's SMC effect bought by the cycle costed
rows.explainer: Our correction, 25% (20% to 50%). The project delivered vitamin A in the last of the season's SMC cycles (October 2021), and the cost per child, $1.18 ($0.9 for SMC alone in the study), is for that one round; the Mali trial's deaths and admissions averted are for a full season of four monthly cycles. Anchor: four cycles a season, so one cycle buys about a quarter of the season's protection; up to half if the late-season cycle matters more.

rows.label: Share of a year's vitamin A effect bought by one dose
rows.explainer: Our correction, 50% (50% to 100%). The 12% fewer deaths is for children supplemented every six months; the sheet applies it to a full year's deaths after the one dose given. Anchor: a dose protects for about six months, which is why programmes give two a year.

rows.label: Healthy years gained, deaths valued by age
rows.formula: (deaths_vas * vas_dose_share + deaths_smc * smc_cycle_share) * death_value_under5 + yld * smc_cycle_share
rows.explainer: All the deaths the sheet counts are of children aged 3 to 59 months, valued the site's way, with the SMC and vitamin A effects cut to what the one round costed buys; within a year, so nothing to discount.

rows.label: Our healthy years for the same deaths and illness, per DALY of The Life You Can Save's
rows.explainer: The evaluator view keeps The Life You Can Save's DALYs (1).

rows.label: Share of the effect that wouldn't have happened without Malaria Consortium
rows.explainer: ×1, our judgment: the sheet credits only the vitamin A and SMC coverage above the baseline and counts the whole cost per child; the SMC baseline it chose (54%, against the 91% monitored) is The Life You Can Save's, kept in both views.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of programme cost
rows.explainer: Default for programmes where staff deliver the help themselves: community distributors go door to door with the drugs and capsules. Our judgment.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Health workers and field staff at nonprofits. Our judgment.

Share of the full cost paid in cash
